# Threadmark launch day

## LinkedIn post

Today we're launching Threadmark, a small desktop app for research folders.

Point it at a folder of PDFs and notes, and it builds a local, searchable evidence map of what you've collected. The launch feature is source-linked summaries. Click any sentence in a summary and it opens the passage that supports it, so you can check the claim against the source instead of trusting the wording.

That check is the point. A summary you can't verify is just a confident guess, and we'd rather you verify it than take our word for it.

Processing stays on your computer. Threadmark runs on Windows and macOS today. Linux is being investigated, but we aren't promising it yet.

It costs $12 a month after a 14-day trial. If you have a literature review sitting in a folder, the trial is a good way to test it on your own papers.

## Bluesky post

Threadmark is live: a local, searchable evidence map for folders of research PDFs and notes. Click a summary sentence to open the passage behind it. Windows and macOS now. Linux is under investigation, not promised.

## Instagram caption

Threadmark launches today.

It's a small desktop app. Point it at a folder of research PDFs and notes, and it builds a searchable evidence map that stays on your computer.

The part we care about most is source-linked summaries. Click a sentence and it opens the passage it came from, so you can check the summary against the paper instead of taking it on faith.

Windows and macOS are available now. Linux is being investigated, but we aren't promising it yet.

There's a 14-day trial, then $12 a month. Try it on the folder you've been avoiding.

#literaturereview #researchtools #academiclife

## Replies

### LinkedIn

**"Is this just another chatbot wrapping my documents?"**

It's a fair question, and the difference is easy to check. Click any sentence in a summary and it opens the passage behind it. If a passage doesn't support the sentence, please message us. That's a bug we want to hear about.

**"Can a university buy seats for a lab?"**

I don't have a lab or group plan to announce, so I can't say yes to seats today. The published price is $12 a month after a 14-day trial. If your lab is weighing it, message us with the number of people and what you need, and we'll tell you honestly whether it fits.

### Bluesky

**"no linux, no deal"**

Fair, if Linux is a requirement for you. Threadmark runs on Windows and macOS now. Linux is being investigated, but I can't promise it or give a date. If you're on one of those two, the 14-day trial lets you test it on your own papers.

**"Does local mean you train on my papers anyway?"**

Local means indexing and processing happen on your computer, so your papers aren't sent to us for that. Anything beyond that is covered in our written data terms, and I'd rather you read those than take my paraphrase. If they leave a question open, reply here and we'll look at it.

### Instagram

**"I paid and the app has been stuck indexing for two hours."**

I'm sorry. Two hours stuck after paying is not the experience we want for you. Please DM us your OS, your app version, and roughly how many files are in the folder, and we'll take it from there. Please keep account and payment details out of the comments.

**"Would this work for a literature review in Japanese?"**

I can't confirm Japanese support yet, so I won't promise it. The 14-day trial is the most direct test, run on a few of your own papers. If you DM us what the folder looks like, we'll tell you what we know and what we don't.

## Before posting (internal)

- Confirm a written data policy exists and says what, if anything, leaves the machine besides indexing (updates, licensing, telemetry). The Bluesky data reply depends on it.
- Confirm the status of lab or group licensing and of Japanese-language support. The replies say neither is settled.
- Confirm someone monitors DMs on Instagram and LinkedIn before the replies go up, since two of them ask people to DM.
- No trial or purchase link was given in the brief, so none is included.

- **Precise, not grandiose.** The source-linked summary carries the pitch. No superlatives, percentages, certifications, or dates.
- **Short, specific apologies.** The outage reply names the problem, owns the wait, and moves account and payment details to DMs.
- **Calm on pushback.** The Linux and data replies state the situation and stop. They neither argue nor reassure.
- **Mildly nerdy.** Concrete nouns ("passage behind the sentence", "local, searchable evidence map") do the work that adjectives would.
- **Platform fit.** LinkedIn gets full sentences, Bluesky stays under 280 characters, Instagram stays brief.
- **No bait or templates.** No calls to comment and no "thanks for your feedback."
